changes.reason: Unpin the entangled conduction states at 5-7 eV, which lie outside the range the criterion scores, so the subspace can be smoother and the hoppings shorter-ranged. The scored range up to E_F+2 eV stays frozen with a 3 eV margin.

diagnosis: The SMV construction with analytic s,p,d projectors on both atoms is correct where it is constrained: the untruncated eta_2 is 0.97 meV, every band check passes, and the centres and spreads are balanced (ratio 1.53). It fails only the sparse criterion, and only just: 20.04 meV against a 20 meV limit. That error comes from the tail of the hoppings, not from fidelity. The fitted decay length is 2.04 Å, and 7.6e-5 of |H|^2 lies beyond r_c = 9.99 Å, spread evenly over the Ga- and As-centred functions. When those hoppings are cut, the largest errors are about 60 meV on valence bands 8 and 9 near (0,½,½) and on the lowest conduction band. The cure is a smoother, more localised subspace. num_bands is already at the maximum the parent allows (27 kept bands), so the remaining freedom is the frozen window. At 7 eV it pins all of bands 10-11, much of bands 12-13 (3.36-9.84 eV) and the bottom of band 14 (from 6.91 eV). These entangled states carry kinks that the gauge cannot smooth away, and they lie well above the E_F+2 eV range the criterion scores. Lowering dis_froz_max to 5 eV still pins every state below E_F+5 eV, so the scored range stays exact. It frees the entangled states at 5-7 eV, so disentanglement can pick a smoother subspace with shorter-ranged hoppings. The non-converged disentanglement (steps steady at about 2.4e-6) also points to a constrained subspace landscape, not a budget problem, so I am not raising the iteration count.
